name: Egypt

facts.religion: Sunni Islam about 90%, Coptic Christian about 10%

snapshot: The Iran war hit Egypt's three cash machines at once, the Suez Canal, tourism and foreign investment, as Sisi tried to stay out of the fight and act as mediator.
culture: Egypt is the Arab world's entertainment capital: Cairo's film and television industry and singers like Umm Kulthum shaped how millions of Arabs speak and what they watch, and Ramadan TV dramas are still a national event. Al-Azhar, founded in 970, is the leading seat of Sunni learning. The Coptic Church, one of the oldest in the world, anchors a large Christian minority.
society: Almost all Egyptians live in the narrow Nile valley and delta, and Greater Cairo has more than 20 million people. The economy has lurched through currency devaluations and IMF bailouts, and inflation has eroded incomes. Huge state and army-run projects, including a new administrative capital, have expanded the military's economic role. Subsidised bread is a political red line.

story: In 1956, Gamal Abdel Nasser nationalised the Suez Canal, and Britain, France and Israel invaded to take it back. Egypt kept it, and the canal became a symbol of independence and, more practically, one of its few reliable sources of hard currency. In its record year, 2022-23, it earned $10.2 billion. Then the Houthis started firing at ships in the Red Sea after the Gaza war began, shipping lines diverted around Africa, and revenue fell by about two-thirds. President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi says the disruption has cost Egypt roughly $10 billion (Alhurra).

Early 2026 looked like recovery: the canal earned $449 million in the first weeks of the year, up 18.5 percent, and tourism hit a record $24 billion in 2025 (Middle East Institute). In February Sisi reshuffled the cabinet, bringing in 13 new ministers including a new defence minister and a World Bank economist as planning minister (AP via The Messenger). Then the US-Israeli war on Iran began on 28 February. Maersk again halted voyages through the Red Sea, freight and insurance costs jumped, tourists cancelled, Israeli gas supplies were interrupted and about $10 billion of foreign portfolio money fled the country (NoonPost). Egypt was better prepared than in past shocks thanks to IMF-backed reforms and big Gulf investment deals, but for 110 million people with little margin, the effect shows up in bread and fuel prices. Sisi has worked to keep Egypt out of the war and positioned it as a mediator.
briefing.power: A presidential republic dominated by the military. The president, a former army chief, is elected for six-year terms in tightly controlled votes and appoints the prime minister; parliament is overwhelmingly loyal. Dissent is heavily repressed.
briefing.holders: President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, in power since 2013; Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly.
